newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian gas will go to Turkey from Port Said area.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian gas will go to Turkey from Port Said area.

text.p: Egypt and foreign oil companies have chosen the Port Said area as the site for a terminal for exports of Egyptian liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Turkey, an Oil Ministry official said on Tuesday.
The government newspaper Akhbar el-Yom on Saturday quoted Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi as saying the terminal would be near the north Sinai town of El Arish, 150 km (90 miles) to the east.
But the official said this report was completely baseless. "It will be in Port Said and we are in talks with Port Said governorate on the exact loaction," he added.
An executive at the U.S. oil company Amoco, a major partner in the oil export project, said: "We're looking at the Port Said area but nothing has been finalised."

"We are narrowing it down to one site that's suitable but there will be quite a bit of dredging to do, wherever you are," he added. The waters off the Nile Delta and north Sinai are shallow right along the coastline.

Under a memorandum of understanding signed in November, Egypt will export up to 10 billion cubic metres of LNG a year by the year 2000. The project is expected to cost between $2 billion and $4 billion.
